plain.text: But God remembered Noah and all the animals with him in the ark. He sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to go down. The springs and the floodgates were closed and the rain stopped. The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. The waters kept going down until the tops of the mountains could be seen.

After forty days, Noah opened a window and sent out a raven, which kept flying back and forth. Then he sent out a dove, but it found nowhere to rest and returned. Seven days later he sent the dove again, and it came back with a freshly picked olive leaf in its beak. Noah knew the water had gone down. After seven more days he sent it out again, and it did not return.
The ground was dry. God told Noah to come out of the ark with his family and all the animals, so they could multiply and fill the earth. So they came out, family by family.

Noah built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings. The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma and said in his heart that he would never again curse the ground because of people, even though every inclination of the human heart is evil from childhood. "As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease."

summary.bigIdea: God remembers Noah, the waters go down, and God promises that the seasons will continue as long as the earth lasts.
points: A dove returns with an olive leaf, a sign of new life.
Noah worships, and God promises seedtime and harvest will never cease.
summary.reflection: Noah's first act on dry land was to worship. How could you thank God after a hard season ends?
